title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has responded to the Committee's 2020 report on artificial intelligence and public standards by outlining measures to increase transparency, accountability, and safety in AI systems. It calls for new regulations, guidance for public‑sector use, and closer collaboration with industry to ensure responsible AI deployment.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is laying out how it will oversee the use of artificial intelligence in exam and assessment settings to ensure fairness, reliability, and transparency. The guidance helps schools, examiners and candidates understand the rules and responsibilities around AI tools used in qualifications.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report evaluates how copyright laws affect the training and use of artificial intelligence, examining legal risks, licensing practices, and potential infringement issues. It also offers impact assessments and policy recommendations for balancing creators’ rights with AI development and innovation.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has issued its reply to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence, outlining how it will address the challenges and opportunities highlighted in the committee’s report on AI in the UK. It emphasizes commitments to investment, regulation, skills development, and international cooperation to ensure AI benefits society while managing its risks.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document explains what the committee will do, how it will operate, and the key responsibilities for reviewing how artificial intelligence fits with public standards, including a FAQ section for stakeholders. It serves as a guide for everyone involved to understand the committee’s purpose, expectations, and the decision‑making process around AI standards.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL submitted written evidence to the UK Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on AI governance, offering its perspective on how AI should be regulated. The submission includes recommendations for policy and oversight to ensure AI is developed and used responsibly.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The document discusses how artificial intelligence will shape the rules and standards for medical products, focusing on safety, effectiveness, and ethical use. It outlines steps for applying the AI White Paper principles to create clear, transparent, and accountable regulatory guidelines for healthcare technologies.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make our defence organisation the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI player in the world, given our size. It outlines how we will develop and deploy AI to strengthen national security while maintaining high standards of reliability and trustworthiness.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Department for Transport will partner with the transport sector to harness artificial intelligence’s potential for improving services, safety, and efficiency. It will also implement measures to identify, assess, and mitigate the risks associated with AI deployment across the industry.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report reviews how copyright works are used in AI system development, assessing compliance with Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It outlines progress made, highlights remaining challenges, and proposes recommendations for responsible use of copyrighted content in AI training.
